sections.heading: Bhavnagar's GIDC Estates: Chitra, Vartej and Sihor
paragraphs: Bhavnagar's organised industry sits in Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation estates run from the GIDC regional office at Vitthalwadi, Udhognagar. In June 2024 that office advertised an e-auction of industrial plots and sheds in three estates of the Bhavnagar region: Chitra on the city's edge, Vartej to the west, and Sihor-II towards Sihor. The listed lots ranged from small sheds of about 140 square metres to plots of more than 2,600 square metres.

That mix matters for tube buyers. A shed-sized unit in Chitra usually needs a few hygienic lines replaced or added and cares about traceable certificates for a small quantity, while a new plot in Vartej or Sihor-II is a full project where the process piping, utility headers and CIP returns are all specified together and drawn up by a fabricator before tube is ordered.

sections.heading: Mahuva's Dehydrated Onion Cluster in Bhavnagar District
paragraphs: The biggest food-processing story in Bhavnagar district is onion dehydration. India Sea Trade News describes Mahuva as the biggest centre for onion processing, with about 120 dehydration plants making powder, flakes, granules and dried cut onion, and new units still being built. Gujarat's exports of dehydrated white onion rose from 50,052 tonnes in 2019-20 to 83,452 tonnes in 2023-24, according to APEDA data, with buyers in the US, Canada, Mexico, the UK, Germany, the Netherlands, France, Spain and West Asia.

Business Standard reported as early as 2014 that Gujarat's onion arrivals are concentrated in the Bhavnagar, Mahuva and Gondal blocks, which is where most dehydration units were set up, and named Maharaja Dehydration in Mahuva among them. Because the product is sold abroad as a food ingredient, these plants work to FSSAI licensing at home and to the hygiene audits their importers run, and both look closely at product-contact surfaces.

Most of a dehydration line is washing, peeling, slicing, belt drying and milling, but stainless tube runs through the wet end and the powder end: wash-water and chlorinated-water dosing lines, transfer of fines, and pneumatic conveying of powder and granules to sifters and packing. Fine onion powder picks up moisture and clings to rough bores, so a smoother internal surface on conveying and transfer tube reduces build-up and shortens the cleaning needed between batches and export lots.

sections.heading: SF1 or SF4 Tube for Mahuva and Bhavnagar Food Plants
paragraphs: For a Mahuva dehydration plant the choice is usually between SF1, a mechanically polished bore per ASME BPE, and SF4, the same tube electropolished after polishing. SF1 in 304L is adequate for dry-product conveying where there is no water, no chlorine and no salt in contact with the steel, and it keeps the cost of long conveying runs down.

SF4 in 316L earns its price on the wet side. Onion wash water is often chlorinated, and Bhavnagar's coastal air carries salt, so any line that is wet, cleaned with chlorinated water, or sits near the washing and peeling area should be 316L. Electropolishing removes the smeared surface layer left by polishing and leaves a chromium-rich passive film, which resists the chloride pitting that shows up first at welds and on the outside of tubes in a damp shed.

Powder lines are the one place where SF4 is worth considering even in a dry service. The lower roughness and the absence of polishing grooves give fine, sticky powder less to hold on to, which helps when an importer's auditor asks how the plant prevents carry-over from one lot to the next. We supply an internal Ra report for each electropolished lot so that the finish can be shown, not only stated.

sections.heading: 316L or 904L on Bhavnagar's Salt and Marine-Chemical Coast
paragraphs: Bhavnagar is a salt and marine-chemicals city. It is home to CSIR-CSMCRI, the Central Salt and Marine Chemicals Research Institute, on Gijubhai Badheka Marg, and Business Standard reported that Nirma commissioned the first stream of its soda ash plant at Bhavnagar in 1999-2000 and the second stream in September 2000. Nirma describes soda ash as made from salt, limestone and ammonia, and its chemicals range also includes bromine and food-grade phosphoric acid.

For tube in this kind of service the grade question is chlorides and acids, not hygiene alone. 316L, with its molybdenum, is the practical minimum for brine, bittern and any line that sees salt-laden water, and SF4 electropolishing adds a cleaner passive layer for sampling, dosing and instrument lines where a pit would contaminate a reading or a batch.

Where a line carries phosphoric acid, dilute sulphuric acid or hot chloride solutions that pit 316L, 904L is the usual upgrade, and we supply 904L electropolished. Send the medium, concentration, temperature and chloride level with the enquiry; the grade is then chosen against the actual duty rather than by habit.

sections.heading: What a Bhavnagar Buyer Should Send in an RFQ
paragraphs: A quotation for a Bhavnagar-district plant comes back faster and more accurately when the enquiry already answers the questions below. We quote within 24 hours of receiving a complete enquiry.
bullets: Which plant and line the tube is for: a Mahuva dehydration unit's wash, transfer or powder-conveying line, or a Chitra, Vartej or Sihor-II unit's process or CIP line.
Grade and finish for each line: 304L or 316L, SF1 or SF4, and whether any chemical, brine or acid line needs 904L electropolished.
Standard and sizes: ASTM A270 or A269 for sanitary and instrument tube, ASTM A249 for welded tube, ASTM A312 for process pipe, with OD, wall and the total length per size.
The documents your auditor or importer asks for: EN 10204 3.1 certificates traced to heat number, PMI on every length, NABL-lab chemical analysis and the Ra report for electropolished lots.
The delivery address in Bhavnagar, Mahuva, Sihor or the estate, and whether the tube goes to the plant or to a fabricator first.
